Alger, 26 novembre 2026 (Algeria Tech) —: Algiers, November 26, 2026 (Algeria Tech) — On the occasion of its AI Day held in Guangzhou on November 25, Xpeng unveiled its VLA 3.0 architecture, a near-final version of its Iron humanoid robot, and a robotaxi project scheduled for 2027. The company also formalized a software update designed to accelerate the charging speed of electric vehicles already on the road.
Les nouveautés techniques et l'évolution: Technical innovations and the evolution of robotics
Lors de sa huitième édition annuelle, la: During its eighth annual edition, the firm presented the VLA 3.0 architecture, an artificial intelligence model based on the Vision-Language-Action principle. This new technical foundation relies on three systems operating at different speeds. System two, the slowest, handles complex task planning and goal decomposition. System one, faster and already present in cars via the VLA 2.0 model, reacts in real-time to the environment. System zero, a novelty in this version, directly controls power, energy, and motors while feeding the machine's physical state back to the other decision-making layers, thereby establishing continuous adaptation.
Le robot humanoïde Iron, doté de soixant: The Iron humanoid robot, equipped with 76 degrees of freedom and over 1,500 tactile sensor points covering 80 percent of the key areas of its body, was also showcased. Xpeng plans to use it as a salesperson in its stores during the first quarter of 2027, ahead of an official release in the second quarter. Furthermore, the brand announced the development of a robotaxi, for which driverless testing has begun in Guangzhou after obtaining a level 4 operating permit.
Du côté des automobiles, le système X-VM: On the automotive side, the X-VMC 2.0 system centralizes propulsion, brakes, steering, and suspensions under the coordination of artificial intelligence. An application called co-driving has been introduced to modulate braking and energy recovery when the driver releases the accelerator, allowing the company to gain 12.4 percent of usable range in urban traffic jams compared to driving without energy recovery.
En outre, une mise à jour à distance per: In addition, an over-the-air update will upgrade models equipped with a 5C battery to 6C. This evolution reduces the charging time from 10 to 80 percent from 12 minutes to 10.7 minutes on compatible vehicles, following endurance tests totaling 1,200,000 hours. Adaptive deceleration will be deployed first in December 2027 in China, while no date has been communicated for Europe regarding 6C charging.
